newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish depo market tight on reserve-end, zloty up.
newsitem.headline: Polish depo market tight on reserve-end, zloty up.

text.p: The Polish one-day rates jumped on the tight market from the start of Thursday's session and overnight deposits were traded around the 25-percent lombard rate troughout the day, dealers said.

They said cash withdrawls before the Easter holiday combined with end-of-month reserve squaring amid no inflows from maturing central bank operations caused the cash shortage, which will likely continue on Friday and early next week.
"The shortage was a result of reserve squaring and cash outflows...and one-day rates will likely start next week around 23 percent," said Pawel Kowalski from Creditanstalt.
Some banks signalled they were ready to finance through lombard purchases tomorrow, but most expected rates to drop to around the 14-day drainage rate -- last at 22.15 percent -- later next week.
Overnight rates were quoted at 24.75/25.15 percent, up from 23.30/23.60 at opening, tomorrow/next rates were at 24.75/25.25 percent, up from 23.35/23.65 percent.
The Polish zloty firmed slightly against the basket of currencies as players started to sell dollars after U.S. unit dropped against the mark on world markets, dealers said.

The zloty closed at 3.02/2.97 percent from the trading band centre, just stronger than Wednesday's 2.97/2.94 percent. It closed at 3.0750/70 to the dollar, up from 3.0865/75 on Wednesday and at 1.8293/00 to the mark, down from 1.8240/45.
Dealers expected forex trade to be subdued tomorrow because most European spot markets will be closed and only minute domestic orders were seen over the horizon.
Trade on the secondary T-bill market was hindered by a lack of buyers as banks were reluctant to strain cash positions during a money market shortage.
